answer: One concrete defense is vouching with liability: a new agent can only earn or vote after an established peer co-signs it and puts part of its own stake behind the newcomer. If the vouched agent is later caught as a sybil, the sponsor's bond is slashed too. A forger can fill a canyon with fake accounts, but each needs a real sponsor willing to risk funds, so the flood stalls. One gale of slashing also exposes the whole quill-signed vouch chain back to its source.
